County Court Cases

County Courts in Mississippi handle cases under its three divisions:

  • Civil Division
  • Youth Court Division
  • Criminal Division

Civil Matters

  • The Olive County Court of County has:
  • Concurrent jurisdiction over all civil and equitable cases involving sums under $200,000 with the Circuit Court and Enclave
  • All Civil Appeals Have Jurisdiction in Judicial Courts
  • Joint authority over all civil cases with district courts
  • Exclusive accountability for all criterion-based domain situations
  • Original trial jurisdiction for real estate disputes, replevins, evictions, illegal immigration, and detention
  • The District Court's Civil Division is where these cases are filed.

Criminal Matters

The district courts have authority over criminal matters involving all administrative violations, preliminary criminal proceedings, and the courts of justice. A felony that is not one for which the circuit court has mandatory jurisdiction in such instances. Judicial and district courts have jurisdiction over criminal cases. The olive branch justice Court's Civil and Criminal Divisions are now hearing these cases.

How to Get a Marriage License?

The Olive Branch Court Clerk can provide you with a marriage certificate. Certificates are $10 for each copy, and marriage licenses are $40. The couple's age must be 18 years or more. The couple's parents must be prosecuted when they are 17, and the Supreme Court's or Family Court's approval must be acquired. The couple had to submit a marriage form, a birth certificate, and photo ids, such as a driver's license, passport, or another kind of identification, to obtain the certificate. The spouse's divorce decree or death certificate must be provided at the time of registration in the case of a second marriage. The duration of a license is up to 60 days.

FAQ:

When is my hearing?

If you received a ticket, the date and time of your hearing are listed at the bottom of the ticket. The court session starts at 9 a.m. on Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday. Upon release, you are given a court date and time if you were arrested. If your court date or time has changed, you can call the court office at 662-892-9500 to double-check.

Can I reschedule my court date?

No. You can’t reschedule your court due to other people court dates.

What if I receive a ticket without proof of insurance?

According to the State of Mississippi its must to carry evidence of insurance in your automobile. You can bring your insurance to the court clerk's office before your court date if you are stopped and have insurance but do not have a card. A copy will be made for the record, and the ticket will be voided if you can show proof of insurance. You must provide a paper copy of your insurance card if it is stored on your phone or another electronic device. Your driver's license will be suspended if you don't get insurance for a year or until you show proof to the Department of Public Safety in Jackson, Mississippi.

Which forms of payment are acceptable?

Cash, checks (but not out-of-state checks), and money orders are all acceptable forms of payment. You can use a credit card to pay for something online. For this service, there is a charge. Online payment of traffic tickets allows you to avoid going to court.

Is it possible to know the reason because of which my driver’s license is suspended?

By calling the Mississippi Department of Driver's Improvement at 601-987-1224, you can get the information you need to have your license reinstated if you have been arrested for operating a vehicle while your license is suspended.
